line: Crowley’s Two of Swords: Peace, ruled by Chokmah in the Element of Air, the Moon in Libra.

sections.title: What Crowley names
sections.line: The old title, Lord of Peace Restored, Crowley calls incorrect; Lord of Peace is the better name. The second quotation gives the element of its suit.

quotes.quote: The Two of Swords was formerly called the Lord of Peace Restored
“Wands”, attributed to Fire; “Cups”, to Water; “Swords”, to Air;

sections.title: Its place on the Tree and in the zodiac
sections.line: The card is ruled by Chokmah in the Element of Air, with the celestial attribution the Moon in Libra.

quotes.quote: This card is ruled by Chokmah in the Element of Air.
the celestial attribution: the Moon in Libra

sections.title: What it figures
sections.line: Crowley reads the Moon as change and Libra as balance, regulating the energy of the Swords.

quotes.quote: The Moon is change, but Nature is peaceful; moreover, Libra represents balance; between them, they regulate the energy of the Swords.
The energy abides above the onslaught of disruption.
